Continued consumption of this type of diet leads to hypercholesterolemia due to the presence of excess amount of saturated fatty acid.

5083.text: Which of the following statement is correct for fcc lattice?

Octahedral voids are present at the body center and edge centers.

5083.sol: (a) There are equal number of octahedral and tetrahedral voids in a unit cell for fcc lattice is incorrect statement. The number of octahedral and tetrahedral void in unit cell for fcc lattice is 4 and 8 respectively. (b) The tetrahedral voids are present at the edge centers is incorrect as they are present on each body diagonal, i.e. diagonal of cubic unit cell. 27815.subject: Chemistry
27815.text: The bond dissociation energy is highest for
27815.sol: Fluorine ( F 2 ) , Chlorine Cl 2 , Bromine Br 2 , Iodine I 2 are called halogen compounds, they occur as diatomic molecules in which a covalent bond is formed after sharing 1 electron with each other. As it moves down from chlorine to iodine in the halogen group, the atomic size increases, and hence bond length also increases. As bond length increases, the energy required to break bonds (dissociation energy) decreases. So, chlorine will have the highest bond energy.

71582.subject: Biology
71582.text: Path of water movement from soil to xylem is
options: Metaxylem Protoxylem Cortex Soil Root hairs Pericycle Endodermis
Soil Cortex Root hair endodermis Pericycle Protoxylem Metaxylem
Soil Root hair Cortex Endodermis Pericycle Protoxylem Metaxylem
Pericycle Soil Root hair Cortex Endodermis Protoxylem Metaxylem
71582.sol: Water is absorbed from the soil by the root hairs present on the epidermis of the root. From the root hairs, water moves deeper into the root layers, passing first through the cortex. After the cortex, water enters the endodermis, which regulates the flow of water into the vascular cylinder. From the endodermis, water passes into the pericycle. Finally, water enters the xylem, first reaching the protoxylem and then the metaxylem. The correct sequence of water movement is: Soil Root hair Cortex Endodermis Pericycle

Lead storage battery and Nickel-Cadmium (Ni-Cd) cell are secondary cells, which can be recharged by passing current through them in the opposite direction. Answer: ( R Z )^2

75875.sol: The Khilafat movement (1919-22) was a pan-Islamic, political protest campaign launched by Muslims in British India to influence the British government. The movement became the reason for separation from mainland India of an Islamic Pakistan, in the process unleashing tremendous separation-trauma, mainly upon ethnic Punjabis. The movement was a topic in Conference of London (February 1920); however, Arabs saw it as threat of continuation of Turkish dominance of Arab lands.

77852.subject: Mathematics
77852.text: How many 7-letter words (with or without meaning) can be constructed using all the letters of the word CAPITAL so that all consonants come together in each word?
77852.sol: The word CAPITAL has 7 letters. Vowels: A, I, A (3 letters, where A is repeated twice) Consonants: C, P, T, L (4 distinct letters) Since all consonants must come together, they are treated as a single unit: (C, P, T, L). Now, there are 4 units to arrange: the consonant group and the 3 vowels (A, I, A). The number of ways to arrange these 4 units is 4! 2! because the letter A appears twice. 4! 2! = 12 The 4 consonants can be arranged among themselves in 4! ways. 4! = 24 Total number of words = 12 24 = 288 Answer: 28

84522.sol: The primary and secondary immune responses are carried out with the help of two special types of lymphocytes present in our blood, ie, B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes. The B-lymphocytes produce an array (a range) of proteins in response to pathogens into our blood to fight with them. These proteins are called antibodies. The T-cells themselves do not secrete antibodies but help B-cells to produce them.

To serve as the site of attachment of spindle fibres
To aid in the condensation of chromosomal material
123603.sol: By this stage, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be observed clearly under the microscope. This then, is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied. At this stage, metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere. Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that

123749.subject: Botany
123749.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The stage between two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis and is generally short lived. Reason: There is no replication of DNA during interkinesis.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
123749.sol: The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis and is generally short lived. There is no replication of DNA during interkinesis.

123952.subject: Botany
123952.text: At what stage of the cell cycle are histone proteins synthesized in a eukaryotic cell ?
options: During G ₂ stage of prophase
123952.sol: Histone proteins are basic proteins and are used in packing of eukaryotic (absent in prokaryotes) DNA. DNA and histones together comprise chromatin, forming bulk of the eukaryotic chromosomes. Histones are of five major kinds H₁, H_ 2 A , H_ 2 B , H₃ and H₄ . H₁ histones link neighbouring nucleosomes (fundamental packing units of an eukaryotic chromosome), while other are elements of nucleosome structure. During S-phase of cell cycle synthesis of histone proteins take place because at this stage number of chromosom

124023.subject: Botany
124023.text: Where are glycoproteins and glycolipids formed?
124023.sol: The golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face. This explains, why the golgi apparatus remains in close association with the endoplasmic reticulum. A number of proteins synthesized by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the golg

124163.subject: Botany
124163.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Leucoplasts are colorless plastids 2. Amyloplasts store proteins 3. Chloroplasts contain cartenoid 4. The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is called the stroma. 5. A number of organised flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids, are present in the stroma
124163.sol: The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients.

124349.subject: Botany
124349.text: Given below are four pairs of cellular structures and their descriptions: (I) Cristae : Infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane (II) Cisternae : Flattened membranous sacs in the stroma of chloroplast (III) Thylakoids : Disc-shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus (IV) Mesosome : Membranous extension into the cytoplasm of prokaryotes How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
124349.sol: (I) Cristae are the infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane. (Correct) (II) Cisternae are the flat, disc-shaped sacs present in the Golgi apparatus, not the chloroplast. (Incorrect) (III) Thylakoids are the flattened membranous sacs present in the stroma of the chloroplast, not the Golgi apparatus. (Incorrect) (IV) Mesosomes are formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell in prokaryotes. (Correct) Therefore, exactly two pairs (I and IV) are correctly matched. Answer: Only two

124453.subject: Botany
124453.text: Accessory sexual character in female is promoted by
124453.sol: Estrogens are secreted by cells of Graafian follicles. Estradiol is the principal feminizing estrogen. It stimulates the development of female secondary sex characteristics during puberty and maintains them through the reproductive years of adult life.

124876.subject: Botany
124876.text: Assertion : When the ambient temperature is high and soil contains excess of water, the plants tend to lose water in the form of droplets from lenticels. Reason : Root pressure regulates the rate of loss of water form lenticels.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
124876.sol: When the ambient temperature is high and soil contains excess water, the rate of transpiration is increased i.e., loss of water takes place from leaves through stomata. Lenticular transpiration is only 0.1 % of the total transpiration. It however continues day and night because lenticels have no mechanism of closure. The lenticels connect the atmospheric air with the cortical tissue of stem through intercellular spaces present amongst the complementary cells. Root pressure regulates the rate of loss of water from t

124880.subject: Botany
124880.text: A human RBC is placed in 1.5 % salt solution. It will
124880.sol: For human RBC , 0.9 % salt solution is isotonic. Hence a medium of 1.5 % salt solution would be hypertonic i.e. more concentrated. Hence, the RBC will shrink due to exosmosis.

125716.subject: Botany
125716.text: Assertion : Deficiency of sulphur causes chlorosis in plants. Reason : Sulphur is a constituent of chlorophyll, proteins and nucleic acids.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
125716.sol: Sulphur is not a constituent of chlorophyll but it helps in chlorophyll formation. Due to the deficiency of sulphur, chlorosis often appears first in the young leaves. Mineral constituent of chlorophyll is magnesium which is situated in the centre of the porphyrin ring.

125935.subject: Botany
125935.text: What occurs when one of the male gametes moves towards the egg cell?
options: It undergoes syngamy with the central cell.
It fuses with the egg cell's nucleus.
It produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.
It forms a diploid primary endosperm nucleus.
125935.sol: After entering one of the synergids, the pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the synergid. One of the male gametes moves towards the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus thus completing the syngamy. This results in the formation of a diploid cell, the zygote. The other male gamete moves towards the two polar nuclei located in the central cell and fuses with them to produce a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) (Figure 1.13a). As this involves the fusion of three haploid nuclei it is

126158.subject: Botany
126158.text: Seed/Pollen Viability A. Pollen(Solanaceae) 1. 2000 years B. Seed(Lupinus Articus) 2. 30 minutes C. Seed(Phoenix Dactifera) 3. Few months D. Pollen(rice) 4. 10,000 years
126158.sol: In some cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release, and in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminoseae and Solanaceae, they maintain viability for months -The oldest is that of a lupine, Lupinus arcticus excavated from Arctic Tundra. The seed germinated and flowered after an estimated record of 10,000 years of dormancy. A recent record of 2000 years old viable seed is of the date palm, Phoenix dactylifera discovered during the archeological excavation at King Herod’s

126232.subject: Botany
126232.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The fertilization process in angiosperms is uniquely termed as double fertilization. Reason (R): Two male gametes are released by the pollen tube, where one fuses with the egg cell and the other fuses with the two polar nuclei. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from th
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
126232.sol: Assertion (A) is true because the phenomenon of two types of fusions taking place in the embryo sac is a unique characteristic of flowering plants (angiosperms), which is termed double fertilization. Reason (R) is true and provides the exact mechanism for this phenomenon. The pollen tube releases two male gametes into the synergid. One male gamete fuses with the egg cell (syngamy) to form a diploid zygote. The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) to form the triploid primary endosperm n

126782.subject: Botany
126782.text: The complex polysaccharide that forms the exoskeleton of arthropods is a homopolymer of which of the following monomeric units?
126782.sol: The exoskeleton of arthropods is made of a complex structural polysaccharide called chitin. According to NCERT, chitin is a homopolymer consisting of N-acetyl glucosamine monomers. Glucose is the monomeric unit for starch, glycogen, and cellulose. Fructose is the monomeric unit for inulin. N-acetyl galactosamine is an incorrect modification of the actual monomer. Answer: N-acetyl glucosamine

126817.subject: Botany
126817.text: In the enzyme which catalyses the breakdown of: H ₂ O ₂ H ₂ O + O ₂ the prosthetic group is :
126817.sol: The enzyme which catalyse the breakdown of H ₂ O ₂ as : H ₂ O ₂ H ₂ O + O ₂ is called Catalase which have prosthetic group Haem. This enzyme is activated by iron. The breakdown occurs inside peroxisome during photorespiration.

127930.subject: Zoology
127930.text: Through which structure does the undigested waste pass out in frogs?
127930.sol: Food is captured by the bilobed tongue. Digestion of food takes place by the action of HCl and gastric juices secreted from the walls of the stomach. Partially digested food called chyme is passed from stomach to the first part of the small intestine, the duodenum. The duodenum receives bile from gall bladder and pancreatic juices from the pancreas through a common bile duct. Bile emulsifies fat and pancreatic juices digest carbohydrates and proteins. Final digestion takes place in the intestine. Digested food is a

128497.subject: Zoology
128497.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons, pass through axons and are released their nerve endings 2. The hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary 3. The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus 4. The hypothalamus is located
128497.sol: The hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons, pass through axons and are released their nerve endings. The hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary. The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus. The hypothalamus is located in the fore brain

128851.subject: Zoology
128851.text: What type of heart do humans possess?
128851.sol: Heart, the mesodermally derived organ, is situated in the thoracic cavity, in between the two lungs, slightly tilted to the left. It has the size of a clenched fist. It is protected by a double walled membranous bag, pericardium, enclosing the pericardial fluid . Our heart has four chambers , two relatively small upper chambers called atria and two larger lower chambers called ventricles

129272.subject: Zoology
129272.text: Match the following options w.r.t diagram shown below: Column I Column II Neurotransmitter Q. released neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors Synaptic vesicles R. Chemicals involved in the transmission of impulses Postsynaptic membrane S. vesicles filled with these neurotransmitters
129272.sol: Chemicals called neurotransmitters are involved in the transmission of impulses at these synapses. The axon terminals contain vesicles filled with these neurotransmitters. When an impulse (action potential) arrives at the axon terminal, it stimulates the movement of the synaptic vesicles towards the membrane where they fuse with the plasma membrane and release their neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft. The released neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors, present on the post-synaptic membrane. This b

129425.subject: Zoology
129425.text: Which cranial nerve has the highest number of branches?
129425.sol: Vagus nerve has five branches (i) Superior laryngeal nerve (ii) Recurrent laryngeal nerve (iii) Cardiac nerve (iv) Pneumogastric nerve (v) Depresser nerve.

129667.subject: Zoology
129667.text: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The medullary zone of the kidney is divided into a few conical masses called medullary pyramids projecting int
Inside the kidney, the cortical region extends in between the medullary pyramids as renal pelvis.
Glomerulus along with Bowman’s capsule is called the renal corpuscle.
Renal corpuscle, proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) and distal convoluted tubule (DCT) of the nephron are situat
129667.sol: Inside the kidney the cortical region extends in between the medullary pyramids as renal columns are called columns of Bertini.

130036.subject: Zoology
130036.text: Mark the true statement among the following with reference to normal breathing
options: Inspiration is a passive process whereas expiration is active
Inspiration is an active process, whereas expiration is passive
Inspiration and expiration are active processes
Inspiration and expiration are passive processes
130036.sol: Inspiration is an active process, whereas expiration is a passive process as no energy is required in expiration.

130372.subject: Zoology
130372.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. In the centre of each ‘I’ band is an elastic fibre called ‘H’ line which bisects it 2. Actin and myosin are called thin and thick filaments. 3. In the resting state a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments. 4. The HMM component, i.e.; the head and short arm projects outwards at regular distance and angle fr
130372.sol: Actin filaments are thinner as compared to the myosin filaments, hence are commonly called thin and thick filaments respectively.,The HMM component, i.e.; the head and short arm projects outwards at regular distance and angle from each other

130901.subject: Zoology
130901.text: What is the process of releasing the secondary oocyte from the ovary called?
130901.sol: The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterized by a fluid filled cavity called antrum. The theca layer is organized into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa. It is important to draw your attention that it is at this stage that the primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle grows in size and completes its first meiotic division. It is an unequal division resulting in the formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body. The secondary ooc

130978.subject: Zoology
130978.text: Label a, b, c, and d from the diagrammatic sectional view of the mammary gland.
options: a - Mammary lobe, b - Mammary alveolus, c - Mammary duct, d - Ampulla
a - Mammary alveolus, b - Mammary lobe, c - Ampulla, d - Mammary duct
a - Mammary duct, b - Mammary lobe, c - Mammary alveolus, d - Ampulla
a - Ampulla, b - Mammary duct, c - Mammary lobe, d - Mammary alveolus

131179.subject: Zoology
131179.text: Which one of the following is not a male accessory gland?
131179.sol: Male accessory glands are the seminal vesicle, prostate gland and bulbourethral gland. Ampulla is a part of the female reproductive system.

131409.subject: Zoology
131409.text: Who proposed the Double Helix model for the structure of DNA?
131409.sol: DNA as an acidic substance present in nucleus was first identified by Friedrich Meischer in 1869. He named it ‘Nuclein’. However, due to technical limitations in isolating such a long polymer intact, the elucidation of structure of DNA remained elusive for a very long period of time. It was only in 1953 that James Watson and Francis Crick, based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin, proposed a very simple but famous Double Helix model for the structure of DNA. One of the h

131446.subject: Zoology
131446.text: What is the difference between the S strain and the R strain of Streptococcus pneumoniae?
options: The S strain is virulent while the R strain is not
The S strain produces smooth colonies while the R strain produces rough colonies
The R strain is virulent while the S strain is not
The R strain produces smooth colonies while the S strain produces rough colonies
131446.sol: In 1928, Frederick Griffith, in a series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae (bacterium responsible for pneumonia), witnessed a miraculous transformation in the bacteria. During the course of his experiment, a living organism (bacteria) had changed in physical form. When Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) bacteria are grown on a culture plate, some produce smooth shiny colonies (S) while others produce rough colonies (R). This is because the S strain bacteria have a mucous (polysaccharide) coat, while

131604.subject: Zoology
options: DNA sequences that code for proteins
DNA sequences that form the basis of paternity testing
Small stretches of DNA that are repeated many times
Satellite DNA sequences that form a major peak during density gradient centrifugation
131604.sol: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in a DNA sequence called repetitive DNA, because in these sequences, a small stretch of DNA is repeated many times . These repetitive DNA are separated from bulk genomic DNA as different peaks during density gradient centrifugation. The bulk DNA forms a major peak and the other small peaks are referred to as satellite DNA. Depending on base composition (A : T rich or G:C rich), length of segment, and number of repetitive units, the satelli

131625.subject: Zoology
131625.text: What does the given figure represent?

131759.subject: Zoology
131759.text: The net electric charge on DNA and histones is:
131759.sol: The net electric charge on DNA is negative and on histones is positive.

131908.subject: Zoology
131908.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In the Human Genome Project, the Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) approach involves sequencing only a fraction of the total genome rather than the entire DNA sequence. Reason (R): The EST approach focuses exclusively on identifying all the genes that are expressed as RNA. In the light of the above st
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
131908.sol: The Human Genome Project utilized two major methodologies. One approach, called Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs), focused solely on identifying all the genes that are expressed as RNA. Because this method specifically targets only the transcriptionally active (expressed) genes, it inherently ignores the vast non-coding and unexpressed regions of the genome, thereby sequencing only a fraction of the total DNA. The other approach, Sequence Annotation, involved sequencing the entire genome (coding and non-coding). There

132673.subject: Zoology
options: A process where all individuals have an equal chance of survival
A mechanism where the environment selects individuals based on their reproductive success
A method by which organisms adapt instantly to environmental changes
A phenomenon where organisms evolve due to random genetic mutations
132673.sol: Those characteristics which enable some to survive better in natural conditions (climate, food, physical factors, etc.) would outbreed others that are less-endowed to survive under such natural conditions . Another word used is fitness of the individual or population. The fitness, according to Darwin, refers ultimately and only to reproductive fitness. Hence, those who are better fit in an environment, leave more progeny than others. These, therefore, will survive more and hence are selected by nature. He called it

132776.subject: Zoology
132776.text: Identify the labels a, b, c, and d in the diagram showing the adaptive radiation of marsupials in Australia.
options: a- Tasmanian Devil, b- Koala, c- Wombat, d- Kangaroo
a- Wombat, b- Tasmanian Devil, c- Koala, d- Kangaroo
a- Kangaroo, b- Wombat, c- Tasmanian Devil, d- Koala

133127.subject: Zoology
133127.text: Organs which differ in origin but perform similar functions :
133127.sol: The organs which have similar function but are different in their structure and origin are called analogous organs. The organs which have same fundamental structure and origin but function may be similar or different, are called homologous organs. The organs which are present in reduced form and do not correspond to the fully developed functional organs to related animals are called vestigial organs.

133374.subject: Zoology
133374.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Wuchereria worms are transmitted through contaminated water and food. Reason: Wuchereria worms are transmitted to humans through the bite of female mosquito vectors.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true
133374.sol: Many fungi belonging to the genera Microsporum, Trichophyton and Epidermophyton are responsible for ringworms which is one of the most common infectious diseases in man. Appearance of dry, scaly lesions on various parts of the body such as skin, nails and scalp (Figure 7.3) are the main symptoms of the disease. These lesions are accompanied by intense itching. Heat and moisture help these fungi to grow, which makes them thrive in skin folds such as those in the groin or between the toes. Ringworms are generally acq

133520.subject: Zoology
133520.text: Drug 'X' is chemically diacetylmorphine, which is synthesized by the acetylation of an extract obtained from a specific plant. Identify the correct plant source of this extract and the specific locations of the receptors for drug 'X' in the human body.
options: Leaves of Cannabis sativa; Receptors are present in the cardiovascular system
Latex of Papaver somniferum; Receptors are present in the cardiovascular system
Latex of Papaver somniferum; Receptors are present in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract
Erythroxylum coca; Receptors are present in the central nervous system
133520.sol: Drug 'X', which is chemically diacetylmorphine, is commonly known as heroin. It is synthesized by the acetylation of morphine. Morphine is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant, Papaver somniferum. Heroin binds to specific opioid receptors, which are located in the central nervous system (CNS) and the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Cannabinoids interact with receptors mainly in the brain and affect the cardiovascular system, while cocaine is obtained from Erythroxylum coca. Answer: Latex of Papaver somniferum;

134144.subject: Zoology
134144.text: What is the purpose of growing lymphocytes from the blood of a patient in gene therapy for ADA deficiency?
options: To deliver functional ADA cDNA into the patient
To detect antibodies synthesized against pathogen
134144.sol: If a person is born with a hereditary disease, can a corrective therapy be taken for such a disease? Gene therapy is an attempt to do this. Gene therapy is a collection of methods that allows correction of a gene defect that has been diagnosed in a child/embryo. Here genes are inserted into a person’s cells and tissues to treat a disease. Correction of a genetic defect involves delivery of a normal gene into the individual or embryo to take over the function of and compensate for the non-functional gene.The first c

134914.subject: Zoology
134914.text: Recombinant DNA molecule can be created normally by cutting the vector DNA and source DNA respectively with:
134914.sol: Option (1) is the correct answer because, unless we cut the vector and the source DNA with the same restriction enzyme, the recombinant vector molecule cannot be created. In options (2), (3) and (4), restriction enzymes are different for cutting the vector DNA and source DNA, so they cannot be the answers.

134942.subject: Zoology
134942.text: Which one of the following statement is not true regarding gel electrophoresis technique?
options: The separated DNA fragments are stained by using ethidium bromide.
The presence of chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured DNA bands on the gel.
Bright orange coloured bands of DNA can be observed in the gel when exposed to UV light.
The process of extraction of separated DNA strands from gel is called elution.
134942.sol: Isolation of the DNA (or gene of interest) followed by the separation of digested fragment of the DNA is one of the crucial steps of Recombinant DNA Technology. The separation is based on the technique called gel electrophoresis. Gel electrophoresis is a method for separation and analysis of macromolecules (DNA, RNA and proteins) and their fragments, based on their size and charge. The separated DNA segments are stained with ethidium bromide for visualisation after exposure to UV light in gel electrophoresis. Brigh

135135.subject: Zoology
135135.text: What is generally believed about competition in closely related species?
options: It occurs only when resources are abundant
It is irrelevant if resources are not limiting
It occurs when they compete for the same limiting resources
It is always beneficial to both species
135135.sol: When Darwin spoke of the struggle for existence and survival of the fittest in nature, he was convinced that interspecific competition is a potent force in organic evolution. It is generally believed that competition occurs when closely related species compete for the same resources that are limiting, but this is not entirely true. Firstly, totally unrelated species could also compete for the same resource. For instance, in some shallow South American lakes, visiting flamingoes and resident fishes compete for their

135138.subject: Zoology
135138.text: Does competition always require limiting resources?
options: Yes, competition only occurs when resources are limiting
No, competition can occur even if resources are not limiting
Yes, but only in terrestrial ecosystems
No, competition never occurs with abundant resources
135138.sol: When Darwin spoke of the struggle for existence and survival of the fittest in nature, he was convinced that interspecific competition is a potent force in organic evolution. It is generally believed that competition occurs when closely related species compete for the same resources that are limiting, but this is not entirely true. Firstly, totally unrelated species could also compete for the same resource. For instance, in some shallow South American lakes, visiting flamingoes and resident fishes compete for their

135198.subject: Zoology
135198.text: Read the following statements and select the correct option. Statement 1: The prickly pear cactus introduced into Australia in early 1920s caused havoc by spreading rapidly into millions of hectares. Statement 2: When certain exotic species are introduced into a geographical area, they become invasive and start spreading fast because the invaded land does not have its natural predators.
options: Statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is incorrect.
Statement 1 is incorrect but statement 2 is correct.
135198.sol: Besides acting as ‘conduits’ for energy transfer across trophic levels, predators play other important roles. They keep prey populations under control. But for predators, prey species could achieve very high population densities and cause ecosystem instability. When certain exotic species are introduced into a geographical area, they become invasive and start spreading fast because the invaded land does not have its natural predators. The prickly pear cactus introduced into Australia in the early 1920’s caused havo

135319.subject: Zoology
135319.text: A population has more young individuals compared to older individuals. What would be the status of the population after some years?
options: It will first decline and then stabilize
135319.sol: If a population has more young individuals compared to older individuals, it will increase.

135478.subject: Zoology
135478.text: Which of the following is a total root parasite?
135478.sol: Rafflesia is a total root parasite, which remains attached to the roots of the host plants and derives all of its nutritions from them. Cuscuta (dodder or amarbel) is a total stem parasite, while Santalum album (sandal wood) is a partial root parasite.

6a13e468688ac6d0667aad56.subject: Biology
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad56.text: Identify the key difference between Anaphase I and Anaphase II during meiotic cell division.
options: Homologous chromosomes separate in Anaphase II, whereas sister chromatids separate in Anaphase I.
The splitting of centromeres occurs in Anaphase II, whereas it does not occur in Anaphase I.
Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores in Anaphase I, but they attach directly to the telomeres in Anaphase
The chromosome number is reduced to half during Anaphase II, whereas it remains the same during Anaphase I.
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad56.sol: During Anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate and move towards opposite poles, but the sister chromatids remain attached at their centromeres. Therefore, the splitting of centromeres does not occur in Anaphase I. During Anaphase II, the centromeres of each chromosome split, allowing the sister chromatids to separate and move towards opposite poles. Thus, the key difference is that the splitting of centromeres occurs in Anaphase II, whereas it does not occur in Anaphase I. Answer: The splitting of ce

6a0e277b165ae1327797b41d.subject: Biology
6a0e277b165ae1327797b41d.text: Consider the following statements regarding the separation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis: I. DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules and are forced to move towards the cathode under an electric field. II. The sieving properties of agarose gel allow smaller DNA fragments to move farther away from the wells than larger fragments. III. The separated DNA fragments can be visualized as bright orange bands
options: Statements I, II and III are correct
Statements II, III and IV are correct
Statements I and IV are correct
Statements III and IV are correct
6a0e277b165ae1327797b41d.sol: DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules due to the presence of phosphate groups. Under an electric field in gel electrophoresis, they move towards the positive electrode, which is the anode, not the cathode. Thus, Statement I is incorrect. The agarose gel acts as a sieve, and the movement of DNA fragments depends on their size. Smaller DNA fragments experience less resistance and move farther away from the wells compared to larger fragments. Thus, Statement II is correct. DNA fragments cannot be seen in visi

6a16f3297cfacf7984f86745.subject: Biology
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86745.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs. Statement II: RNA polymerase II transcribes the 28S, 18S, and 5.8S rRNAs in the eukaryotic cell. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86745.sol: In eukaryotes, there are three major types of RNA polymerases: RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, and 5.8S). RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA). RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs). Therefore, Statement I is correct, while Statement II is incorrect because RNA polymerase I (not II) transcribes 28S, 18S, and 5.8S rRNAs. Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

96073.subject: Botany
96073.text: I. ER is also called the control center of the cell. II. It modifies chemicals that are toxic to the cell. III. SER is a major site for the synthesis of proteins. IV. ER is a network of interconnected cisternae, tubules, and vesicles present in the endoplasm. Which of the following statement is/are not true about the ER.
96073.sol: ER is a single membrane-bounded structure that forms a channel-like structure in the cytoplasm. 96344.sol: During late prophase, the nuclear membrane disappears and chromosomes are scattered in the cytoplasm. 96509.subject: Botany
96509.text: How many trophic levels are there in a food chain?
96509.sol: Plants represent the first trophic level and the herbivores make the second trophic level. The primary carnivores constitute the third trophic level, and the secondary carnivores, such as large fish, man, etc. constitute the fourth trophic level of an ecosystem.

96661.subject: Botany
96661.text: Out of the total energy received by herbivores from producers, how much is passed to carnivores?
96661.sol: According to the 10% law given by Raymond Lindeman, at each trophic level, only10% of the energy received is transferred to the next trophic level.

97023.subject: Botany
97023.sol: Fruits are mostly formed after fertilization, there are some species in which fruits develop without fertilization such fruits do not bear any seed like seedless grapes, banana, seedless watermelon, Seedless capsicum, seedless pears and some citrus varieties. These plants mainly propagate asexually. Seedless fruits have an increased proportion of edible part than in normal fruits

97174.subject: Botany
97174.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Shoot apices those modify themselves into flowering apices, cannot perceive photoperiods.
Sugarbeet, cabbage and carrots are monocarpic plants.
To initiate flowering, LDP must be exposed to light for a period less than critical duration.
Ethephon causes thinning of cotton, cherry & walnut.
97174.sol: Long Day Plants (LDP) requires exposure to light for a period exceeding critical duration to induce flowering. Ethephon hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples and accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry, walnut). Shoot apices those modify themselves into flowering apices, cannot perceive photoperiods. Biennial monocarpic plants that flower and then die in the second season. Some examples are sugar beet, cabbage, carrot, etc

97192.subject: Botany
97192.text: Select the odd one with respect to long-day plants.
97192.sol: The term long-day describes plants that begin forming flower buds when the days are longer than their critical day length (e.g., spinach, wheat, radish, beet, lettuce, mentha, poppy are examples of long-day plants). Sunflower is a day-neutral plant.

306704.text: Identify the correct statements from the following:
options: A diode valve can operate as an amplifier.
A triode valve can operate as a rectifier.
A triode valve can operate as an amplifier.
A diode valve can operate as a rectifier.
306704.sol: A diode valve consists of two electrodes (cathode and anode). It allows unidirectional flow of electrons (from cathode to anode) and thus can operate as a rectifier. 6a7a1ff8794a12684b5911fc.sol: NO is a non-metal oxide which is neutral in nature. BaO is an alkaline earth metal oxide, which is basic in nature.
